title: Offline pickup counters for a DTC beverage brand
business_task: Analyze whether a direct-to-consumer beverage brand should open offline pickup counters inside partner convenience stores.
company_context: The brand sells functional bottled drinks online with same-day delivery in two large cities. Repeat purchase is healthy, but delivery fees hurt low-ticket orders. A convenience-store chain offered shelf-adjacent pickup counters in 25 stores for a three-month pilot.
available_facts: Average online order value is 210000 VND.
Gross margin before delivery subsidy is about 42 percent.
Delivery subsidy averages 24000 VND per order.
The proposed partner charges a fixed monthly counter fee plus a handling fee per pickup order.
The brand has no previous offline operations team.
Customer surveys show some buyers want cheaper small-basket purchases during commute hours.
The pilot would require daily inventory replenishment and unsold stock handling.
constraints: Do not invent foot traffic or conversion numbers.
Focus on the pilot design, not a national rollout.
Protect brand experience and cold-chain quality.
